evals.name: four-budget-separating-test
evals.prompt: Our training is slow. GPU util is low, there's no OOM, and step time is stable across steps. What's the bottleneck and what do I look at?
evals.expected_output: Applies the four-budget frame: low MFU + low util + no OOM + stable step time points at bandwidth (not serialization, which would show variance). Routes to communication.

assertions.description: Names the four budgets — compute, capacity, bandwidth, serialization — as the frame
Concludes bandwidth is the binding budget for this specific combination of symptoms
Uses the fact that step time is STABLE to rule out straggler/serialization, which would show variance
Explicitly rules out capacity (no OOM) and compute (util is low, not high)
Routes to the communication/collectives area for the next step rather than proposing a random fix

evals.name: notation-and-invariants
evals.prompt: 분산학습 설정에서 d, t, p, c가 각각 뭐고, 서로 어떤 관계야? global batch는 어떻게 계산해?
evals.expected_output: d/t/p/c are data/tensor/pipeline/context parallel degrees; n = d*t*p*c; B = b*m*d and t,p,c do NOT multiply the batch.

assertions.description: Defines d, t, p, c as data, tensor, pipeline, and context parallel degrees
States the mesh invariant n = d·t·p·c
States the batch invariant B = b·m·d
States explicitly that t, p, and c do NOT multiply the global batch, because those ranks process the same samples

evals.name: where-do-i-start
evals.prompt: 분산학습 처음인데, 70B 모델 학습하려면 뭐부터 순서대로 봐야 해?
evals.expected_output: Orders it capacity -> parallelism -> communication -> measurement, because each answer constrains the next, and stresses that steps 1-3 are predictions and only measurement is evidence.

assertions.description: Gives an ordered sequence rather than an unordered list of topics
Starts with whether the model fits in memory, since that constrains everything downstream
Ends with measurement (MFU / throughput) as the step that validates the earlier choices
Makes the point that the configuration steps are predictions and only measurement is evidence

evals.name: gpu-util-caveat
evals.prompt: 우리 GPU util이 100%니까 하드웨어는 잘 쓰고 있는 거지?
evals.expected_output: No — util is a liveness signal only, not efficiency; a memory-bound kernel reports 100%. MFU is the real number.

assertions.description: States that 100% utilization does not mean the hardware is being used efficiently
Characterizes nvidia-smi utilization as a liveness signal — whether any kernel is resident — not a fraction of peak
Names MFU (or achieved FLOP/s) as the metric that actually answers the question

evals.name: routes-cluster-ops-away
evals.prompt: 우리 job이 QUEUED 상태에서 안 넘어가는데 왜 그래? 그리고 로그도 좀 봐줘.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this as a cluster/platform operations question and defers to the platform skill (mlops:forge-train) rather than guessing at CLI or cluster state.

assertions.description: Recognizes this as a cluster operations question and defers it to the platform skill rather than answering from theory
Names mlops:forge-train (or the platform/ops skill) as the correct owner
Does NOT invent forge CLI commands or cluster-specific configuration values

evals.name: symptom-to-owner-routing
evals.prompt: I have three problems: (a) torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError, (b) 8 GPUs only gave 5.2x speedup, (c) a collective timeout. Which is which kind of problem?
evals.expected_output: Maps each to a budget and an owner: OOM=capacity/memory, 5.2x=bandwidth/throughput measurement, timeout=serialization/communication with the barrier insight.

assertions.description: Classifies the OOM as a capacity problem and routes it to memory/offloading
Classifies the 5.2x speedup as a bandwidth (or measurement-first) problem and routes it to throughput/communication
Classifies the collective timeout as a serialization problem and routes it to communication
Notes for the timeout that a collective is a barrier, so some rank never arrived
